newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF bond issue 3.5 times oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: AGF bond issue 3.5 times oversubscribed.

text.p: French insurer AGF said on Thursday a 4.4 billion franc issue of subordinated convertible bonds it launched earlier this week was 3.5 times oversubscribed.

The 3.50 percent coupon bond with a maturity of 13 years and two months was issued at a price of 220 francs and can be converted by the holder into one AGF share. It offers a yield to maturity, if not converted, of 5.77 percent.
The company said that the bond issue would be earnings positive rather than dilutive as some insurance analysts had said they had feared.
Company finance director Laurent Mignon said the issue would be earnings positive as it would allow the company to invest money in new insurance activities.
He noted that the return on capital invested in AGF's insurance operations was 7.7 percent in 1996.

"Thus on this still weak base, the impact of the investment of the subordinated bond would have been earnings positve, boosting the profit per share by 6.5 percent after the theoretical conversion of the bonds," the company said.
